notesStmt.note: The three poems on this sheet were all first published in periodicals in 1888, the first in the September issue of The Century Magazine, the second and third in the New York Herald on 21 May and 16 April, respectively. Whitman was forced to withhold publishing "Old Age's Lambent Peaks" in November Boughs, since he had sold it to the magazine but it had not yet appeared when he was preparing the poetry section of that volume during the summer months. This corrected proof sheet was apparently prepared, therefore, as part of a separate process, in which Whitman ordered small-run printings of short poems to use as mementos, sometimes adding handwritten signatures and/or minor corrections.

note.p: Following its publication in the The Century, "Old Age's Lambent Peaks" was included in the "Sands at Seventy" annex to Leaves of Grass. "To Get the Final Lilt of Songs" appeared under the title "The Final Lilt of Songs" in the Herald and retitled when Whitman republished it in November Boughs (1888) and in subsequent printings of Leaves of Grass. "A Carol Closing Sixty-Nine" was also reprinted, unchanged, in November Boughs and late issues of Leaves of Grass.

div.head: OLD AGE'S LAMBENT PEAKS.

lg.l:
The touch of flame—the illuminating fire—the loftiest look
at last,

O'er city, passion, sea—o'er prairie, mountain, wood—the
earth itself;
The airy, different‸,/ c/hanging hues of all, in falling twilight.,,/
Objects and groups, bearings, faces, reminiscences;
The calmer sight—the golden setting, clear and broad:

So much i' the atmosphere, the points of view, the
situa-
tions situations,δ whence we scan,

Bro't out by them alone—so much (perhaps the best) un-
reck'd unreck'd before;
The lights indeed from them—old age's lambent peaks.

lg.head: A CAROL CLOSING SIXTY-NINE.
lg.l: A carol closing sixty-nine—a resume—a repetition,
My lines in joy and hope continuing on the same.,/
Of ye‸,/ O God, Life, Nature, Freedom, Poetry;

Of you‸,/ my Land—your rivers, prairies, States—you, mot-
tled mottled Flag I love‸,/

Your aggregate retain'd entire—Of north, south, east and
west, your items all;
Of me myself—the jocund heart yet beating in my breast,

The body wreck'd, old, poor and paralyzed—the strange in-
ertia inertia falliun/g pall-like round me;
The burning fires down in my sluggish blood not yet extinct.,/
The undiminish'd faith—the groups of loving friends.

lg.head: TO GET THE FINAL LILT OF SONGS.
lg.l: To get the final lilt of songs,

To penetrate the inmost lore of poets—to know the mighty
ones,
Job, Homer, Eschylus, Dante, Shakspere, Tennyson, Emerson;

To diagnose the shiftli/ng-delicate tints of love and pride ‸and doubt—to
truly understand,
To encompass these, the last keen faculty and entrance-pricce,
Old age‸,/ and what it brings from all its past experiences.
